description: I'm interested in building practical AI-powered solutions, especially agentic AI, LLMs, RAG, and full-stack development. For this hackathon, I'm planning to work on an AI-Powered Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer, where we'll build an intelligent mission control agent equipped with tools and a NASA-based knowledge base to help astronauts handle mission scenarios, monitor resources, and respond to emergencies.
summary:
JAMT, Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer, is an interactive web based training platform that simulates astronaut mission management. It combines a FastAPI backend, React frontend, mission simulation engine, NASA focused knowledge base, retrieval augmented generation, and an AI Mission Control Assistant.
Users manage missions by monitoring oxygen, water, food, energy, fuel, astronaut health, emergencies, and mission progress. They can repair equipment, rest, conduct experiments, and advance mission days while observing the consequences of their decisions.
JAMT makes complex space mission concepts accessible through hands on simulation. Its grounded AI assistant provides guidance based on live mission data and NASA knowledge, while fallback responses keep the system usable when AI services are unavailable. The project supports STEM education, develops decision making and resource management skills, and helps learners understand the challenges of long duration space exploration.
details:
JAMT is a browser based astronaut training simulator where users create missions, monitor spacecraft resources, respond to emergencies, and make decisions that affect mission success. The backend uses FastAPI and Python to manage missions, resources, astronaut health, actions, emergencies, progress, and reports. The frontend uses React, Vite, and JavaScript to provide an interactive mission dashboard and an AI Mission Control Assistant.

The assistant combines NASA knowledge with live mission information to provide grounded guidance. A retrieval system searches NASA related data, while OpenRouter provides AI responses when available. If the AI service is unavailable, the application uses reliable fallback responses so users can continue training.

The project is creative because it turns space mission planning into an interactive learning experience. Users can experiment with different decisions and immediately see their effects. The intended impact is to improve STEM learning, critical thinking, resource management, emergency response, and interest in space exploration.

The project was developed with Python, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, SQLite, React, Vite, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS. The team considered usability, realistic mission constraints, safety, clear feedback, API reliability, offline fallback behavior, data privacy, and the importance of keeping AI responses grounded in trusted information.
